content: The enzyme CYP3A4 plays a critical role in the metabolism of various drugs. When co-administering elagolix with other medications, it is essential to monitor and adjust therapy as needed due to its effects on hepatic and intestinal enzyme activity. Below are detailed interactions and recommendations for specific drugs: 1. Fostemsavir and Elagolix: Fostemsavir increases the levels or effects of elagolix by inhibiting OATP1B1/3 transporters. Avoid co-administration if possible, or adjust the dose of OATP1B1/3 substrates. Monitor closely. 2. Elagolix and Gefitinib: Elagolix decreases gefitinib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor therapy closely and consider increasing the dose of CYP3A substrates if needed. 3. Elagolix and Glasdegib: Elagolix reduces glasdegib levels via CYP3A4 induction. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. Consider increasing the dose of CYP3A substrates. 4. Elagolix and Glecaprevir/Pibrentasvir: Elagolix can both increase and decrease the levels of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir through P-glycoprotein (MDR1) and CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor therapy closely and adjust as necessary. 5. Elagolix and Guanfacine: Elagolix decreases guanfacine levels by inducing CYP3A4. Monitor therapy and consider dose adjustments. 6. Elagolix and Haloperidol: Elagolix reduces haloperidol levels via CYP3A4 induction. Monitor therapy and adjust the dose of CYP3A substrates if needed. 7. Elagolix and Hydrocodone: Elagolix decreases hydrocodone levels by inducing CYP3A4. Monitor therapy closely and consider increasing the dose of CYP3A substrates. 8. Elagolix and Hydrocortisone: Elagolix increases hydrocortisone levels through P-glycoprotein (MDR1) transport. Use caution and monitor therapy. 9. Elagolix and Hydroxyprogesterone Caproate: Elagolix decreases hydroxyprogesterone caproate levels via CYP3A4 induction. Monitor therapy and adjust the dose of CYP3A substrates as needed. 10. Elagolix and Ibrutinib: Elagolix reduces ibrutinib levels by inducing CYP3A4. Monitor therapy closely and consider dose adjustments. 11. Elagolix and Idarubicin: Elagolix increases idarubicin levels through P-glycoprotein (MDR1) transport. Use caution and monitor therapy. 12. Idelalisib and Elagolix: Idelalisib increases elagolix levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration of elagolix 200 mg BID with strong CYP3A inhibitors for more than one month. Limit elagolix to 150 mg daily for up to six months if co-administered. 13. Elagolix and Ifosfamide: Elagolix affects ifosfamide levels through both CYP2C19 inhibition and CYP3A4 induction. Monitor therapy closely and adjust doses as needed. 14. Elagolix and Imatinib: Elagolix can both increase and decrease imatinib levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) and CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor therapy and adjust doses accordingly. 15. Elagolix and Imipramine: Elagolix increases imipramine levels by inhibiting CYP2C19. Use caution with sensitive CYP2C19 substrates. 16. Elagolix and Indinavir: Elagolix can both increase and decrease indinavir levels through P-glycoprotein (MDR1) and CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor therapy closely and adjust doses as needed. 17. Norethindrone Acetate and Insulin: Norethindrone acetate decreases the effects of insulin (including degludec, aspart, and inhaled forms) through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor glucose tolerance. 18. Elagolix and Irinotecan: Elagolix can both increase and decrease irinotecan levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) and CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor therapy closely and adjust doses as needed. 19. Elagolix and Isavuconazonium Sulfate: Elagolix decreases isavuconazonium sulfate levels by inducing CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor therapy. 20. Isoniazid and Elagolix: Isoniazid increases elagolix levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid co-administration of elagolix 200 mg BID with strong CYP3A inhibitors for more than one month. Limit elagolix to 150 mg daily for up to six months if co-administered. 21. Elagolix and Ixabepilone: Elagolix reduces ixabepilone levels by inducing CYP3A4. Monitor therapy and adjust doses as needed. 43. For all interactions, it is critical to monitor the patient’s response and adjust therapy as needed.
